{{Short description|Abstract structure modeling spaces of probability measures}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Giry monad''' is a construction that assigns to a [[measurable space]] a space of [[probability measure]]s over it, equipped with a canonical [[sigma-algebra]].<ref name="giry">{{harvp|Giry|1982}}</ref><ref name="avery">{{harvp|Avery|2016|pages=1231-1234}}</ref><ref name="jacobs">{{harvp|Jacobs|2018|pages=205-106}}</ref><ref name="fritz">{{harvp|Fritz|2020|pages=19-23}}</ref><ref name="moss-perrone">{{harvp|Moss|Perrone|2022|pages=3-4}}</ref> It is one of the main examples of a [[probability monad]].

It is implicitly used in [[probability theory]] whenever one considers [[probability measure]]s which depend [[measurable function|measurably]] on a parameter (giving rise to [[Markov kernel]]s), or when one has ''probability measures over probability measures'' (such as in [[de Finetti's theorem]]).

Like many iterable constructions, it has the [[category theory|category-theoretic]] structure of a [[monad (category theory)|monad]], on the [[category of measurable spaces]].

==Construction==

The Giry monad, like every [[monad (category theory)|monad]], consists of three structures:<ref name="giry-construction">{{harvp|Giry|1982|page=69}}</ref><ref name="riehl">{{harvp|Riehl|2016}}</ref><ref name="perrone">{{harvp|Perrone|2024}}</ref>

* A [[functor]]ial assignment, which in this case assigns to a measurable space <math>X</math> a space of probability measures <math>PX</math> over it;
* A [[natural transformation|natural map]] <math>\delta_X:X\to PX</math> called the ''unit'', which in this case assigns to each element of a space the [[Dirac measure]] over it;
* A [[natural transformation|natural map]] <math>\mathcal{E}_X:PPX\to PX</math> called the ''multiplication'', which in this case assigns to each ''probability measure over probability measures'' its [[expected value]].

===The space of probability measures===

Let <math>(X, \mathcal{F})</math> be a [[measurable space]]. 
Denote by <math>PX</math> the set of [[probability measure]]s over <math>(X, \mathcal{F})</math>. 
We equip the set <math>PX</math> with a [[sigma-algebra]] as follows. First of all, for every measurable set <math>A\in \mathcal{F}</math>, define the map <math>\varepsilon_A:PX\to\mathbb{R}</math> by <math>p\longmapsto p(A)</math>. 
We then define the sigma algebra <math>\mathcal{PF}</math> on <math>PX</math> to be the smallest sigma-algebra which makes the maps <math>\varepsilon_A</math> measurable, for all <math>A\in\mathcal{F}</math> (where <math>\mathbb{R}</math> is assumed equipped with the [[Borel sigma-algebra]]).
<ref name="giry-construction"/>

Equivalently, <math>\mathcal{PF}</math> can be defined as the smallest sigma-algebra on <math>PX</math> which makes the maps 
:<math>p\longmapsto\int_X f \,dp</math> 
measurable for all bounded measurable <math>f:X\to\mathbb{R}</math>.<ref>{{harvp|Perrone|2024|page=238}}</ref>

The assignment <math>(X,\mathcal{F})\mapsto (PX,\mathcal {PF})</math> is part of an [[endofunctor]] on the [[category of measurable spaces]], usually denoted again by <math>P</math>. Its action on [[morphisms]], i.e. on [[measurable map]]s, is via the [[Pushforward measure|pushforward of measures]]. 
Namely, given a measurable map <math>f:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math>, one assigns to <math>f</math> the map <math>f_*:(PX,\mathcal {PF})\to(PY,\mathcal {PG})</math> defined by 
:<math>f_*p\,(B)=p(f^{-1}(B))</math> 
for all <math>p\in PX</math> and all measurable sets <math>B\in\mathcal{G}</math>.
<ref name="giry-construction"/>

===The Dirac delta map===

Given a measurable space <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math>, the map <math>\delta:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(PX,\mathcal{PF})</math> maps an element <math>x\in X</math> to the [[Dirac measure]] <math>\delta_x\in PX</math>, defined on measurable subsets <math>A\in\mathcal{F}</math> by<ref name="giry-construction"/> 
:<math>
\delta_x(A) = 1_A(x) =
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if }x\in A, \\
0 & \text{if }x\notin A.
\end{cases}
</math>

===The expectation map===

Let <math>\mu\in PPX</math>, i.e. a probability measure over the probability measures over <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math>. We define the probability measure <math>\mathcal{E}\mu\in PX</math> by
:<math>
\mathcal{E}\mu(A) = \int_{PX} p(A)\,\mu(dp)
</math>
for all measurable <math>A\in\mathcal{F}</math>.
This gives a measurable, [[natural transformation|natural]] map <math>\mathcal{E}:(PPX,\mathcal{PPF})\to(PX,\mathcal{PF})</math>.<ref name="giry-construction"/>

====Example: mixture distributions====

A [[mixture distribution]], or more generally a [[compound distribution]], can be seen as an application of the map <math>\mathcal{E}</math>. 
Let's see this for the case of a finite mixture. Let <math>p_1,\dots,p_n</math> be probability measures on <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math>, and consider the probability measure <math>q</math> given by the mixture 
:<math>
q(A) = \sum_{i=1}^n w_i\,p_i(A)
</math>
for all measurable <math>A\in\mathcal{F}</math>, for some weights <math>w_i\ge 0</math> satisfying <math>w_1+\dots+w_n=1</math>. 
We can view the mixture <math>q</math> as the average <math>q=\mathcal{E}\mu</math>, where the measure on measures <math>\mu\in PPX</math>, which in this case is discrete, is given by 
:<math>
\mu = \sum_{i=1}^n w_i\,\delta_{p_i} .
</math>
More generally, the map <math>\mathcal{E}:PPX\to PX</math> can be seen as the most general, non-parametric way to form arbitrary [[mixture distribution|mixture]] or [[compound distribution]]s.

The triple <math>(P,\delta,\mathcal{E})</math> is called the '''Giry monad'''.<ref name="giry"/><ref name="avery"/><ref name="jacobs"/><ref name="fritz"/><ref name="moss-perrone"/>

==Relationship with Markov kernels==

One of the properties of the [[sigma-algebra]] <math>\mathcal{PF}</math> is that given [[measurable space]]s <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math> and <math>(Y,\mathcal{G})</math>, we have a [[bijection|bijective correspondence]] between [[measurable function]]s <math>(X,\mathcal{F})\to(PY,\mathcal{PG})</math> and [[Markov kernel]]s <math>(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math>. This allows to view a Markov kernel, equivalently, as a measurably parametrized probability measure.<ref>{{harvp|Giry|1982|page=71}}</ref>

In more detail, given a measurable function <math>f:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(PY,\mathcal{PG})</math>, one can obtain the Markov kernel <math>f^\flat:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math> as follows,
:<math>
f^\flat(B|x) = f(x)(B)
</math>
for every <math>x\in X</math> and every measurable <math>B\in\mathcal{G}</math> (note that <math>f(x)\in PY</math> is a probability measure). 
Conversely, given a Markov kernel <math>k:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(Y,\mathcal{G})</math>, one can form the measurable function <math>k^\sharp:(X,\mathcal{F})\to(PY,\mathcal{PG})</math> mapping <math>x\in X</math> to the probability measure <math>k^\sharp(x)\in PY</math> defined by 
:<math>
k^\sharp(x)(B) = k(B|x)
</math>
for every measurable <math>B\in\mathcal{G}</math>. 
The two assignments are mutually inverse.

From the point of view of [[category theory]], we can interpret this correspondence as an [[adjunction (category theory)|adjunction]] 
:<math>
\mathrm{Hom}_\mathrm{Meas} (X,PY) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_\mathrm{Stoch} (X,Y)
</math>
between the [[category of measurable spaces]] and the [[category of Markov kernels]]. In particular, the category of Markov kernels can be seen as the [[Kleisli category]] of the Giry monad.<ref name="jacobs"/><ref name="fritz"/><ref name="moss-perrone"/>

==Product distributions==

Given [[measurable space]]s <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math> and <math>(Y,\mathcal{G})</math>, one can form the measurable space <math>(PX,\mathcal{PX})\times (PY,\mathcal{PY})=(X\times Y, \mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{G})</math> with the [[product sigma-algebra]], which is the [[product (category theory)|product]] in the [[category of measurable spaces]]. 
Given [[probability measure]]s <math>p\in PX</math> and <math>q\in PY</math>, one can form the [[product measure]] <math>p\otimes q</math> on <math>(X\times Y, \mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{G})</math>. This gives a [[natural transformation|natural]], [[measurable map]] 
:<math>
(PX,\mathcal{PF})\times (PY,\mathcal{PG})\to \big(P(X\times Y), \mathcal{P(F\times G)}\big)
</math>
usually denoted by <math>\nabla</math> or by <math>\otimes</math>.<ref name="fritz"/>

The map <math>\nabla:PX\times PY\to P(X\times Y)</math> is in general not an isomorphism, since there are probability measures on <math>X\times Y</math> which are not product distributions, for example in case of [[correlation]].
However, the maps <math>\nabla:PX\times PY\to P(X\times Y)</math> and the isomorphism <math>1\cong P1</math> make the Giry monad a [[monoidal monad]], and so in particular a commutative [[strong monad]].<ref name="fritz"/>

==Further properties==

* If a measurable space <math>(X,\mathcal{F})</math> is [[standard Borel space|standard Borel]], so is <math>(PX,\mathcal{PF})</math>. Therefore, the Giry monad restricts to the [[full subcategory]] of standard Borel spaces.<ref name="giry"/><ref name="fritz"/>
* The [[algebra for a monad|algebra]]s for the Giry monad include [[compact topological space|compact]] [[convex set|convex]] subsets of [[Euclidean space]]s, as well as the extended positive real line <math>[0,\infty]</math>, with the algebra structure map given by taking [[expected values]].<ref>{{harvp|Doberkat|2006|pages=1772-1776}}</ref> For example, for <math>[0,\infty]</math>, the structure map <math>e:P[0,\infty]\to [0,\infty]</math> is given by 
:<math>
p \longmapsto \int_{[0,\infty)} x\,p(dx)
</math>
:whenever <math>p</math> is supported on <math>[0,\infty)</math> and has finite expected value, and <math>e(p)=\infty</math> otherwise.

==Finitary variant==
There is a finitary version of the Giry monad, here denoted <math>F</math> which maps a set <math>S</math> to the set of [[convex combinations]] on <math>S.</math> Thus, for example, if <math>S = \{a, b, c\}</math>, the formal combination <math>0.2a + 0.2b + 0.6c</math> would be contained in <math>FS</math>.
